name: Pleatcowl
description: Hold one short blade in each fist with the knuckle guards forward and the elbows tucked over the ribs.

name: Kept Hiltfold
description: Cross both blades above the head in an X so that a downward blow slides off the crossed edges.

name: Quick Snapcut
description: The lead blade thrusts straight at the throat line with the shoulder driving behind the point.

name: Narrow Clipper
description: Chop with the rear blade at the opponent's wrist the instant the lead blade has drawn the guard aside.

name: Winghop
description: Slide the front foot a short pace toward the opponent while both blades stay level and the stance stays narrow.

name: Upward Shearing
description: Throw the fist forward so the knuckle guard strikes first and the blade edge follows across the same line.

name: Holding Swingguard
description: Set the guard bar flat against an incoming cut and let the thick steel of the hilt take the blow.

name: Pulling Edgepair
description: Catch the opposing blade behind the knuckle guard and drag it a hand's width off its line.

name: Flurrybump
description: A quick rap of the guard rim on the back of the opponent's fingers that loosens a weapon grip.

name: Shifting Doublehilt
description: Slip a half step to the open side while the guard hand rides the opponent's blade out of the way.

name: Towing Flurry
description: Drive the knuckle guard onto the opponent's forearm and keep pressing so the weapon arm cannot rise.

name: Nabbing Cheekhilt
description: Spin the blade in the palm from forward grip to reverse so the point vanishes behind the forearm.

name: Gnawing Wristside
description: Sweep the reversed blade along the line of the forearm to open the opponent's belly as you pass.

name: Raised Fliptang
description: Fold the arm so the reversed blade lies along it and the elbow forms a shell against blows.

name: Narrow Crossing
description: Rake the reversed blade down the opponent's lead arm from the shoulder to the wrist.

name: Holding Shearedge
description: Turn the back to the attacker and let the reversed blades carry a strike harmlessly over the shoulder.

name: Downward Snapcut
description: From behind the forearm the point darts out to stab where the opponent's guard has just opened.

name: Stepping Scissor
description: Shuffle sideways in short paces with the blades back so the opponent cannot read the hands.

name: Pleatlid
description: Roll both wrists in tight circles to wind an opponent's blade away from its line of attack.

name: Scutebump
description: A cut thrown entirely from the snap of a conditioned wrist with almost no arm swing.

name: Mothwedge
description: Brace the blade against the hardened forearm and shove a cut aside with the whole arm.

name: Downward Clipper
description: Release a coiled forearm in a springing thrust that covers more distance than the arm seems to allow.

name: Tight Cheekhilt
description: Lock both wrists together in front of the chest and hold the crossed blades steady against pressure.

name: Mothstrike
description: Four quick cuts follow each other from alternating wrists while neither elbow leaves the ribs.

name: Platepoint Lid
description: Turn a wrist under the opposing blade and pin it against the guard of the other sword.

name: Easing Wristside
description: Spring back one short pace after a thrust so the recovered blades are already in guard.

name: Wingblow
description: Thrust along a body-wide corridor with the elbows pinned so that nothing catches on the sides.

name: Sudden Shearedge
description: Duck under a low rafter and cut across the shins from the crouch with one short stroke.

name: Flurryskitter
description: Use a fixed edge of furniture as the axis and pivot around it to reach the opponent's flank.

name: Shortedge Husk
description: With the back to a wall the elbow and blade together stop any blow from the open side.

name: Scutedash
description: Slip between two bodies and cut the nearer one across the arm before the gap closes.

name: Mothcowl
description: Pin the opponent's weapon hand against a door frame with the guard and hold it there.

name: Angled Shortedge
description: Stand with the left foot and left blade forward and the right blade held back as cover.

name: Shifting Flurry
description: Change which foot and blade lead by one smooth step so the stance is never caught in the swap.

name: Fliptang Dash
description: Count a steady rhythm of left jab then right jab so the two blades never move together.

name: Scutestay
description: Meet a blow with the near blade while the far blade shadows it ready to take a second.

name: Pleatwedge
description: Draw slow circles with the lead blade so any thrust meets steel and slips outward.

name: Scutedrop
description: A thread of qi drawn to the edge before the cut makes the blade bite a little deeper.

name: Hard Shearing
description: Narrow the qi to the point and jab so the tip passes through padding that would stop plain steel.

name: Tight Swingguard
description: Breathe in time with the guard so a thin sheet of qi runs along the crossed blades.

name: Wingstrike
description: After the first blade cuts the second follows its path a heartbeat later and widens the wound.

name: Deep Doublehilt
description: Let qi run along the knuckle guard to feel the pressure of an opposing blade through the steel.

name: Platepoint Hop
description: Lift the body with a brief qi pulse in the legs and enter the opponent's reach in one quiet step.

name: Ready Hiltfold
description: Turn the opposing blade with a smooth qi-backed sweep of the near sword and answer at once.

name: Skipping Scissor
description: Pivot on the rear foot like a hinge so the whole body swings a pace toward the opponent.

name: Backward Crossing
description: Reverse the hinge and swing the body a pace away while both blades keep facing the opponent.

name: Flat Edgepair
description: As the body swings on its hinge the blade follows the arc like a door and cuts across the line.

name: Planted Doublehilt
description: Pivot out of a thrust and let the nearer blade sweep it wide before the other blade replies.

name: Blunt Crossing
description: Slide along the hinge turn into a jab that reaches the flank the opponent has just uncovered.

name: Pulling Snapcut
description: Close the pair of blades like a hinge onto the opposing blade and trap it between them.

name: Leaden Edgepair
description: The edge hand opens with a cut across the chest while the guard hand stays in cover.

name: Hooding Swingguard
description: The guard hand catches the answering blow on its crossbar and holds the line.

name: Upward Hiltfold
description: On a signal beat the two hands swap jobs and the guarding blade becomes the cutting one.

name: Pleatpause
description: Lift the guard blade on a slant so a descending cut skids off toward the open side.

name: Mothlid
description: Break the steady alternating rhythm with a late jab so the opponent's guard lands too early.

name: Locking Wristside
description: Trap the opponent's blade under the guarding sword and cut at the freed arm with the other.

name: Pleatbump
description: Bring the cut back along its own path with the rear edge so the strike lands twice.

name: Skipping Fliptang
description: Glide one pace to the side in rhythm with the swap so the footwork hides the change of blades.

name: Descending Shortedge
description: Both blades swing outward together from a crossed guard and cut the two sides at once.

name: Flurrystrike
description: Both blades snap inward from the open position and shear whatever lies between their edges.

name: Snug Cheekhilt
description: Fold the blades back against the forearms like closed wings and take a blow on the steel.

name: Measured Wristside
description: One slow breath for each opening and closing of the blades builds a steady flow of qi into the cut.

name: Scissor Pace
description: Land softly on the ball of the foot after the shear and settle the blades back to guard.

name: Mothhop
description: Drop the shoulder and slip beneath a long weapon's swing to land inside its useful reach.

name: Fixing Shearedge
description: Keep one blade touching the opposing steel and slide along it toward the hand.

name: Upward Snapcut
description: Hook the edge around the opponent's guard from the inside and cut the arm behind it.

name: Pushing Platepoint
description: Press the shoulder into the opponent's chest while both blades hold the arms out of play.

name: Wingdash
description: Thrust from hip height without winding up so the point lands before a long blade can retreat.

name: Snug Platepoint
description: Hold the two blades in a low slanted roof over the head to shed a descending strike.

name: Easing Hiltfold
description: Push off the inside foot and leave the clinch in one pace before the opponent can grip.
